extractionNotes: EXTRACTION COMPLETE - full document read sequentially via 'pdftotext -f 25 -l 110 -layout' (pages 25-110, main body plus a short tail re-read of 108-110), preceded by a front-matter read (pages 1-24) for the Scope-and-Sequence summary tables and definitions. Written in three incremental saves (Year One; Year Two incl. the 3-option branch; Year Three incl. the 3-option branch) per the incremental-save convention. FINAL TOTALS: 29 Content Standards / 29 Learning Outcomes / 89 Learning Indicators / 89 Assessments across 12 Strand entries (2 shared Strands x 2 years [Year 1 has no pathway split at all] + 1 branching Strand x 3 options x 2 years = 4 + 2 + 6 = 12). Per-pathway breakdown: shared/non-branching content (pathway=null, Strands 'Conceptual Drawing' and 'Geometry', Years 1-3) = 21 CS/21 LO/63 LI; Option 1 ('Extended Drawing' > 'Building Drawing') = 3 CS/3 LO/10 LI across Years 2-3; Option 2 ('Extended Drawing' > 'Mechanical Drawing') = 3 CS/3 LO/8 LI; Option 3 ('Extended Drawing' > 'Garment Design Technology') = 2 CS/2 LO/8 LI. A learner following any one option end-to-end therefore covers: Option 1 = 21+3=24 CS/24 LO/73 LI; Option 2 = 24 CS/24 LO/71 LI; Option 3 = 23 CS/23 LO/71 LI. Cross-check against the document's own Scope-and-Sequence table: Year 1 (7/7/23) matches exactly. Year 2-3 Option 1 table states 17/17/48 (this file's Option-1 Year2+3-only total, i.e. excluding the shared Year-1 numbers, is 17 CS/17 LO/50 LI - CS and LO match exactly, LI is +2 due solely to the documented Year-2 Fractal Geometry anomaly below). Option 2 table states 17/17/46 (this file: 17/17/48, same +2 anomaly). Option 3 table states 16/16/46 (this file, Year2+3 only: 16/16/48, same +2 anomaly - the anomaly reproduces identically across all three options because the anomalous Fractal Geometry Sub-Strand is itself shared/non-branching). In every option, subtracting the 2 anomalous Learning Indicators (2.2.3.LI.3 and 2.2.3.LI.4, both flagged NEEDS_REVIEW below) reconciles this file's counts with the document's own printed Scope-and-Sequence totals exactly, for CS, LO, and LI alike.

STRUCTURAL FINDING (branching pathway): this subject's Scope-and-Sequence section (PDF pages 20-23, printed 21-23) prints THREE alternative summary tables labelled 'Design and Communication Technology Summary - Option 1', '- Option 2', '- Option 3' for Years 2-3. Cross-checking those tables' per-sub-strand CS/LO/LI cell counts (recovered despite heavy column-collision in raw -layout text extraction, by summing candidate splits against each table's own printed row/column totals until they reconciled) against the actual body content confirmed: Strand 1 (Conceptual Drawing) and Strand 2 (Geometry) are IDENTICAL/shared across all three options for both Year 2 and Year 3 (single non-branching sequence, pathway=null) - only Strand 3 ('Extended Drawing') differs by option, and only in Years 2-3 (Year 1 has no Strand 3 at all). Strand 3 has exactly one Sub-Strand per option: Sub-Strand 1 'BUILDING DRAWING' = Option 1, Sub-Strand 2 'MECHANICAL DRAWING' = Option 2, Sub-Strand 3 'GARMENT DESIGN TECHNOLOGY' = Option 3 - printed back-to-back in the body with no 'OPTION' heading anywhere outside the Scope-and-Sequence tables themselves (confirmed via full-document grep for 'option', 0 hits in body Subject/Strand/Sub-Strand headers). Per the task instructions, each option's Strand-3 content is represented as its own Strand object (name 'EXTENDED DRAWING', classLevel SHS2/SHS3) with pathway set to the exact Scope-and-Sequence table title wording: 'Option 1', 'Option 2', 'Option 3'.

Body-vs-table cross-check (Year 2/3, all three options) matches the Scope-and-Sequence table's per-substrand CS/LO/LI cell counts exactly for every sub-strand EXCEPT Year 2 Strand 2 Sub-Strand 3 (FRACTAL GEOMETRY, code prefix 2.2.3): the table states CS1/LO1/LI2 for this sub-strand (consistent across all three options' tables, since it is shared/non-branching), but the body prints FOUR Learning Indicators (2.2.3.LI.1 through LI.4, each with its own AS code) under the single 2.2.3.CS.1 Content Standard, not two. The extra 2.2.3.LI.3 ('Draw orthographic views of given objects') and 2.2.3.LI.4 ('Design artefact with loci') read as near-duplicates of 2.2.1.LI.1 ('Draw orthographic projections of given objects') and 2.2.1.LI.3 ('Design an artefact using the principle of loci') from the Year 2 PLANE GEOMETRY sub-strand two sub-strands earlier, strongly suggesting a copy-paste/duplication error in the source PDF's Fractal Geometry block rather than genuine new content. Removing exactly these 2 LIs reconciles the body count with the table for every one of the three options' overall totals (Option 1 17/17/48->body Y2 total would be 28 not 26 with the extra 2, etc. - full arithmetic verified across all three options). Preserved verbatim in this file (not deleted/fabricated away) and flagged NEEDS_REVIEW on both LIs with a reviewNote.

Curriculum-code non-uniqueness (same documented pattern as Agricultural Science, per the canonical schema's Revision #2): several Sub-Strands print TWO Content Standards under two separate Learning Outcomes (e.g. 2.2.2 Solid Geometry Y2: CS.1 'solid geometry' under LO.1, CS.2 'AutoCAD' under LO.2; 2.3.1/2.3.2 Building/Mechanical Drawing Y2: CS.1 'building/mechanical drawing' under LO.1, CS.2 'Electrical drawings' under LO.2), and in every such case the printed Learning Indicator and Assessment codes RESTART at .LI.1/.AS.1 for the second Content Standard instead of continuing the sequence (e.g. 2.2.2.LI.1 is printed twice - once under 2.2.2.CS.1 and again, for different content, under 2.2.2.CS.2). The natural key is therefore (Year, Strand, SubStrand, ContentStandard, Seq), not the printed code string alone. All such LIs/Assessments are flagged NEEDS_REVIEW with a reviewNote identifying the colliding sibling.

Content Standard description copy-paste error: 2.3.2.CS.1 (Year 2, Strand 3 Extended Drawing, Sub-Strand 2 MECHANICAL DRAWING/Option 2) is printed with the description 'Understand the concept of building drawing' - identical to sibling sub-strand 2.3.1.CS.1's description (Building Drawing/Option 1) - even though every one of 2.3.2.CS.1's own Learning Indicators is about sectional/mechanical drawing, not building drawing. Preserved verbatim; flagged NEEDS_REVIEW.

Genuine verbatim duplication (not flagged as an error, only noted for visibility): the 'Electrical drawings' Content Standard (2.3.1.CS.2 under Building Drawing/Option 1 and 2.3.2.CS.2 under Mechanical Drawing/Option 2) is printed with essentially word-for-word identical description, Learning Indicator, and pedagogical-exemplar text in both Sub-Strands - this reads as intentionally shared cross-option content (both options' learners cover the same electrical-drawing basics) rather than a scanning error, so it is preserved as two distinct nodes (one per option/Strand-3 entry) without a NEEDS_REVIEW flag.

Teaching and Learning Materials (this document's in-body label, distinct from the front-matter glossary's 'Teaching and Learning Resources' term - see docs/inventory-parts/design-communication-technology.md) are attached at the CONTENT STANDARD level (one bullet/table block printed at the end of each Content Standard's Learning-Indicator block), matching Geography's attachment point, not the Sub-Strand level - teachingLearningResources/teachingLearningResourcesHeaderSeen fields are on each contentStandards[] node.

Page/pdfPageIndex convention: printed footer 'DESIGN AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY | N' pages consistently map to pdfPageIndex = N + 2 (verified against the raw pdftotext page-by-page extraction, e.g. printed page 23 = pdf page 25, printed page 107 = pdf page 109, the final content page before the document ends). learningIndicators.description: Analyse the sources and use of templates and patterns in the community.

contentStandards.description: Apply the concept of plane geometry in designing.

learningIndicators.description: Explain types of plane geometrical figures and give examples.
pedagogicalExemplars: Talk for Learning/ Experiential learning/ collaborative learning: 1. With the aid of relevant pictures, cardboard charts and objects in the school environment, engage learners to brainstorm in whole class discussion to come out with the meaning of plane geometry. 2. learningIndicators.description: Explain sectioning in relation to building codes, standards and symbols.
pedagogicalExemplars: Research, Collaborative learning/ Group work: With relevant resources engage learners in mixability groups to discuss sectioning and its relevance to the building industry.

Experiential learning, managing talk for learning: 1. Show to learners a model of a cross section through a domestic building showing all the sectional members. 2. Instances where a model is not available, you may consider a virtual form. 3. Assist learners to identify the sectional parts discussed earlier on the model.

contentStandards.description: Understand the concept of Mechanical drawing.
teachingLearningResources: charts and drawing instruments (such as set-squares)

learningIndicators.description: Explain the principles of assembling component parts.
pedagogicalExemplars: Research, Managing talk for learning: 1. With the use of internet surfing, YouTube videos, pictures, charts and board illustrations, review learners' knowledge on sectional drawing in year two. 2. Engage learners in group discussion to outline the types of assembly drawings and explain them. 3. Assist the learners to come out with a comprehensive report from their research on the types, uses and explanation of assembly drawings in a whole class discussion.

dokDescriptions: Level 4 Extended critical thinking and reasoning

learningIndicators.description: Prepare assembly drawing from component parts.
pedagogicalExemplars: Experiential learning, Activity-based learning: 1. Let learners look around in the classroom, outside the classroom and mention some objects or artefacts they see. 2. Write the names of the objects or artefact on the board and help learners identify the parts making the objects or the artefact mentioned. 3. Ask learners to find out the quantity of each part, give each item/part a number and make a bill of materials for the parts.

Activity-based learning: 1. Guide learners to measure the parts and draw them using the appropriate drawing tools. Through YouTube videos, board illustrations, charts and simulations, demonstrate the assembly drawing of the parts first in a picture form, then in section to show the interior view of the parts and then the exploded view also to show the flow of the assembly of the parts. 2. Assist learners to prepare assembly drawing to scale using the appropriate drawing tools.

pedagogicalExemplars: Managing talk for learning, Activity-based learning: 1. Use board illustrations, pictures, and charts to engage learners in a whole class discussion to explain detailed working drawing. 2. Demonstrate the preparation of detailed working drawing with the use of board illustrations, charts, videos and pictures in a whole class. 3. Prepare detailed working drawings of a given machine part or system to scale using appropriate drawing instruments and CAD.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding and techniques in conceptual and geometrical drawings in designing garments.

learningIndicators.description: Grade patterns to different sizes.
pedagogicalExemplars: Group work/Collaborative Learning: Let learners in groups explain pattern grading in different sizes using the standard size charts through the use of videos, photographs, drawings, and charts and present their findings in a whole class discussion.

Research, Group work, Experiential learning: Help learners in their groups to find out the importance of grading patterns in sizes with the use of internet surfing, videos, photographs and drawings. Let the learners examine the various garment sizes that can be graded during garment design and pattern making. Generate a manual or digital chart of grading, sizing and their importance/uses. Present their reports in a whole class discussion.
Project based learning, Group work: Pair learners and ask them to identify their various partners sizes on the standard size chart and make patterns for them using a base pattern as a guide.

dokDescriptions: Level 4 Extended critical thinking and reasoning

learningIndicators.description: Examine garment designs to break patterns down into different components.
pedagogicalExemplars: Group work/Collaborative Learning: Let learners in groups examine garment designs and describe the various style lines or details in them. Assist learners to break down garment designs into various components indicating the pattern symbols through the use of videos, photographs, drawings and charts. Let them present their findings in a whole class discussion.

Research, group work: Help learners in their groups to find out the importance of garment design examination with the use of internet surfing, videos, photographs, drawings, etc. Assist learners to break down examined style lines or details into different components. Generate a manual chart on garment design examination and pattern breakdown with their importance/uses. Present report in a whole class discussion.

Collaborative Learning, research, experiential learning: In mixed groups, let learners identify various garment design examinations and components of pattern breakdown during garment design. Prepare a manual report to be presented in a whole class discussion.

Project based learning, Group work: Pair learners and ask them to identify various garment designs from different sources to examine the style lines or details and break them down into different components with the appropriate pattern drafting tools.

dokDescriptions: Level 4 Extended critical thinking and reasoning

learningIndicators.description: Manipulate patterns to make adaptations of different garment designs.
pedagogicalExemplars: Group work/Collaborative Learning: Let learners in groups explain pattern design manipulation and adaptations through the use of videos, photographs, drawings, charts etc. Present their findings in a whole class discussion.

Research, group work: Help learners in their groups to find out the relevance of pattern design manipulation and adaptation with the use of internet surf, videos, photographs, drawings, etc. Generate a manual chart on pattern design manipulation and adaptation with their relevance/uses. Present report in a whole class discussion.

Collaborative Learning, research, communication, experiential learning: In mixed groups, let learners examine pattern designs and use their findings for manipulation and adaptation during garment design and pattern making. Prepare a manual report to be presented in a whole class discussion.

dokDescriptions: Level 4 Extended critical thinking and reasoning

learningIndicators.description: Make Pattern adjustments and alterations.
pedagogicalExemplars: Group work/Collaborative Learning: Let learners in groups explain pattern adjustments and alterations through the use of videos, photographs, drawings, charts etc. Present their findings in a whole class discussion.

Research, group work: Help learners in their groups to find out the importance of pattern adjustments and alterations with the use of internet surf, videos, photographs, drawings, etc. Generate a manual chart on pattern adjustments and alterations with their importance/uses. Present report in a whole class discussion.

Collaborative Learning, research, experiential learning: In mixed groups, let learners examine pattern adjustments and alterations during garment design and pattern making. Prepare a manual report to be presented in a whole class discussion.

Project based learning, Group work: Pair learners and ask them to identify different garment fitting problems and discuss how they can be adjusted and altered using their knowledge in pattern adjustment and alterations.
